# zufft

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zufft/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zufft/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedrobtz/zufft/main/.github/badges/coverage.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zufft/actions/workflows/coverage.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

zufft computes fast Fourier, cosine and sine transforms in R. It bundles the
BSD-licensed FFT code of [ducc0](https://github.com/mreineck/ducc), the same
subset and commit that SciPy uses, so it needs no system FFTW library and
carries no GPL code.

Its goals, in order:

1. **Replace fftwtools without FFTW.** Install with `install.packages()`
   alone, under a permissive licence.
2. **Perform like fftwtools.** Within 1.5 times its speed everywhere, and
   faster on prime lengths, many simultaneous transforms and threads.
3. **An easy, familiar API.** Function names a fftwtools user recognises,
   with the conventions of `scipy.fft` for axes, normalisation, cosine and
   sine transforms, and threads.

> **Status (2026-10-13): not yet usable.** The package is being built stage
> by stage; see the [roadmap](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zufft/blob/main/.agents/roadmap.md) and the
> [v0.1.0 issue](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zufft/issues/2).

## Installation

You can install the development version of zufft from
[GitHub](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zufft) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zufft")
```
